findings.finding: The plan says that adding `code_review` to `_gate_sidecar_fields` stops it from 'silently dropping sidecar provenance for code_review'. That rests on a false premise: no code-review path produces the fields `_gate_sidecar_fields` copies. `_gate_sidecar_fields` reads only `sidecar_emitted`, `sidecar_reviewed_at` and `runner == "reused"`. Those first two fields are written only by plan_review (sidecar.py:94, reuse.py, orchestrator.py, claimability.py, __init__.py:668) and completion_sidecar.py:229-249. `rebar.llm.review_code` / `_verdict_to_review_result` never sets them, and its runner is 'code-review-gate', not 'reused'. The MCP `review_code` also passes no `target_ticket`, so no ticket-anchored code_review sidecar is emitted at all. `_review_result_status` in gate_runs.py also depends on `_GATE_SIDECARS` plus a non-empty ticket_id, which a code_review job (empty ticket_id by design) does not have.
findings.location: Design bullet '_gate_sidecar_fields reads a GATE_TYPES_WITH_SIDECARS constant that includes code_review'; AC3 '_gate_sidecar_fields no longer silently drops sidecar provenance for code_review'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a failure-disposition contract per arm for `transition` and `code_review` jobs: gate FAIL = permanent, ConcurrencyError = retryable, provider throttle/error = retryable (WAIT_AND_RETRY/INDETERMINATE), daemon death = stated status. Make the disposition a structured `gate_status` field, not just `error` text.
evidence: "A completed transition settles `passed` with verdict `applied`; a refusal (gate FAIL, ConcurrencyError) settles `failed` with the message in `error`."
"so a provider failure is the same structured result on both"
No retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent wording appears for any arm.
findings.finding: The plan adds new failure arms but states no disposition contract for them. A `transition_ticket_start` refusal collapses a gate FAIL (permanent until the work changes) and a ConcurrencyError (transient, and retryable by re-firing) into the same `failed` status, with only free-text `error`. Nothing says what surfaces when the verifier or code-review provider throttles or errors inside the daemon (INDETERMINATE / WAIT_AND_RETRY vs fatal). Nothing says how a daemon that dies mid-job (after the gate, before or after the append) is reported. For `review_code`, the plan only says a provider failure is 'the same structured result' on both surfaces, without naming its disposition.
findings.location: Design — transition_ticket_start ("a refusal (gate FAIL, ConcurrencyError) settles `failed` with the message in `error`") and review_code_start ("a provider failure is the same structured result on both")
scenarios: A ConcurrencyError surfaces as `failed`, so an agent treats it like a verifier FAIL and stops instead of re-firing.
A Bedrock throttle in the daemon verifier surfaces as `failed`, which masks a retryable condition as a terminal refusal.
The daemon is killed after the gate passed. The job status and the actual ticket status disagree, and the plan names no disposition for that case.

findings.finding: The review_code_start dedup key uses the raw symbolic base/head strings (defaults 'HEAD~1'/'HEAD'). Its basis comes from ref=None, which resolve_basis_sha turns into origin/main, not the reviewed head. If HEAD moves while a review is running, a new review request attaches to the stale run of the old range. That is the same defect class as bugs 3b27-8f4b / c912-f274 that the material-keyed variants fixed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests: (a) a gate-FAIL `transition_ticket_start` close settles `failed` and the ticket stays `in_progress`; (b) a re-fire while in flight returns the same `job_id` with exactly one gate invocation, for both new starters; (c) at least one test runs the transition through the real `_spawn_gate_daemon` path, including spec hooks.

findings.finding: The testing plan covers only the happy path and the asynchrony property. AC4 drives each starter to 'a terminal state' and checks that the handle returned early. No AC tests the refusal path: a `transition_ticket_start` close whose gate FAILs must settle `failed` and leave the ticket `in_progress`. AC2 itself requires 'applies the status change only on gate success', but nothing verifies it. AC7's attach-on-re-fire (same `job_id`, one gate run) has no stated test. Nothing requires the test to run the wrapped derived tool, with its spec pre/post hooks, inside the actually spawned daemon rather than an in-process substitute. A substitute would bypass the riskiest new path: rebuilding and executing a write tool in the daemon.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Say how transition_ticket_start (and review_code_start) relate to _mcp_health's CERTIFIED/SIGNING/DRAINED_TOOLS: either refuse new starts while draining, or record that daemon-hold accounting is the intended drain behavior.

findings.finding: `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` keeps the SIGTERM-drain classification (CERTIFIED_TOOLS, SIGNING_TOOLS, DRAINED_TOOLS). transition_ticket is listed in SIGNING_TOOLS specifically because a close signs a completion certificate (bug external-taxonomic-iguanodon). transition_ticket_start moves that signing close onto a daemon, and the plan never says how the new surface fits this classification. As written: the async starter can't be added to DRAINED_TOOLS, because instrument_certified_tools raises on async tools. Its daemon is counted only through gauge.hold, which never refuses while draining. So during a drain a new close is accepted instead of getting the MCPRetiringError that sync transition_ticket returns. The plan should make and record this decision, in the plan or in the docstring of `_mcp_health.py`.

findings.location: Why the existing workaround does not cover it / Design: transition_ticket_start

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that `review_code_start` and the singleflight key resolve `base`/`head` to commit SHAs before computing the dedup key.
evidence: "a dedup variant carrying `base`/`head`/`source`"
findings.finding: The `review_code_start` dedup variant carries `base`/`head` but does not say whether symbolic refs are resolved to commit SHAs before keying. If keyed on raw refs, a re-fire after HEAD moves could attach to a review of a different commit range.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the full code_review verdict vocabulary (PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE) for the job record and say how an INDETERMINATE or llm_ran=False result settles (failed with coverage.llm_error in `error`, or passed with an explicit degraded flag).
evidence: Plan: "`_terminal_from_result` unwraps the nested code-review verdict dict to its PASS/BLOCK string"
src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:328-355 `_degraded_code_review_verdict` returns {"verdict": "INDETERMINATE", ... "coverage": {"llm_ran": False, "llm_error": ..., resolution fields}}
src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:170-173: only a truthy `error` key yields `failed`; anything else is `passed`
src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py:90-94: review_result nests the gate verdict under `verdict` and copies `coverage` to the top level, with no `error` key
findings.finding: The code-review verdict vocabulary is incomplete. The plan says `_terminal_from_result` unwraps the nested code-review verdict 'to its PASS/BLOCK string', and AC1 says the job settles carrying 'the review's PASS/BLOCK verdict'. But the code-review gate also emits `INDETERMINATE` on an outage or mid-run failure, and that result has no top-level `error` key. Under the current `_terminal_from_result` rule (no `error` means `passed`), a degraded code review that never ran would settle as `passed` with verdict INDETERMINATE. The plan gives no fallback for that case.
scenarios: A provider outage during review_code_start: gate_status reports status=passed with verdict=INDETERMINATE, and a poller that treats `passed` as 'review completed' moves on without a real review.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Design bullet, specify: an unwrapped code-review verdict of INDETERMINATE (or coverage.llm_ran == False) settles `failed`, with `error` = coverage.llm_error, and retryable/resolution_class are surfaced on the record. Add that case to AC1/AC4.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the `transition` durable verdict as the ticket's current status matching the requested target (plus cert currency only for close), and state the behavior for non-close transitions.
evidence: "`gate_runs._durable_verdict` maps a `transition` job to the ticket's completion-certificate currency, so a close poller sees whether the completion cert persisted."
"a refusal (gate FAIL, ConcurrencyError) settles `failed`"
findings.finding: The durable verdict for `transition` jobs measures the wrong thing. `gate_runs._durable_verdict` maps a `transition` job to the ticket's completion-certificate currency. But the cert can be persisted (verifier PASS, signed) while the transition itself was refused, for example by a ConcurrencyError, so a poller sees a 'durable PASS' for a close that never applied. Also, `transition_ticket_start` wraps the full `transition_ticket` tool, so non-close transitions such as `open -> in_progress` can also run as `transition` jobs. For those, completion-cert currency is meaningless or stale.
scenarios: Verifier PASS persists the cert, then the append loses a ConcurrencyError. The job is `failed`, but the durable view shows the completion cert as current, which contradicts it.
`transition_ticket_start(open->in_progress)` reports a durable completion-cert currency that has nothing to do with the requested transition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make a transition job's durable field report the ticket's current status against the requested target (plus completion-cert currency only when the close required a cert), so a poller can confirm the transition applied even after the run index is lost.
evidence: Plan: 'maps a transition job to the ticket's completion-certificate currency, so a close poller sees whether the completion cert persisted'
close_precheck returns completion_expectation values 'gate_off', 'force_bypassed', 'disposition', 'local_source', 'not_certifiable', which close without a completion signature
gate_runs.gate_status materializes stale running records as failed
findings.finding: Reporting a transition job's durable result as 'the ticket's completion-certificate currency' answers a different question from 'did the transition apply'. Many valid closes write no completion cert: gate off, force-bypassed, disposition, local source, not certifiable, idea rejection. Non-close transitions never do. When the daemon dies and gate_status turns a stale running record into failed, the cert field cannot tell a poller whether the status write actually committed.
scenarios: A force close or administrative close finishes, the server restarts, and gate_status reports failed with durable verdict 'unsigned'. The caller re-fires a close on an already-closed ticket.
transition_ticket_start(X, in_progress→open): the durable completion field is irrelevant.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the requested from/to in the run index. In _durable_verdict for 'transition', return {status: <current ticket status>, applied: current == target, completion: verify_completion_status(...) if target == 'closed'}.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the sync `transition_ticket` close through `run_gate_singleflight` with the same `transition` key as `transition_ticket_start`, and extend AC7 to cover a sync re-fire attaching to an in-flight run.
evidence: "the natural response is to re-fire the same call -- a second billable gate pass."
"the sync tool goes through `run_gate_singleflight` with the same key" — stated only for review_code.
AC7: "de-dup protection applies to the new surfaces"
findings.finding: The symptom is three successive re-fires of the SYNC `transition_ticket` close, each a potential billable gate pass. But AC7 dedup covers only the 'new surfaces', and the design does not route the sync `transition_ticket` close through `run_gate_singleflight` (as it explicitly does for sync `review_code`). The original double-billing hazard therefore persists for any caller still using the sync tool.
scenarios: An older agent or client calls sync transition_ticket to close, times out, and retries; each retry re-runs the verifier.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether a close with a current signed completion certificate (same SHA) should skip the inline verifier, diagnose why the measured close still ran long, and either fix cert reuse or document that `transition_ticket_start` will wait on or attach to an in-flight `verify_completion` run for the same ticket instead of starting a second one.
evidence: "`transition_ticket` with that signed certificate in place -> **timed out again**."

"It uses its own gate type `transition`, not `verify_completion`: the dedup key starts with the gate type, so reusing `verify_completion` would let a close ATTACH to a running `verify_completion_start`..."
The plan does not say why a current, signed certificate does not short-circuit the close gate, or whether that is intended.
findings.finding: The plan's own evidence shows a duplicate billable gate run that the design does not close off. After `verify_completion_start` passed and signed a certificate at the same SHA, `transition_ticket` still timed out. So the close path re-runs the completion verifier instead of consuming the fresh certificate. The design then gives `transition_ticket_start` its own `transition` dedup key, so it never attaches to an in-flight `verify_completion_start`. It also does not state that the close will reuse a current signed certificate. An agent following the old guidance (verify_completion_start, then close) still pays for two full verifier passes, and the two may run concurrently.
findings.location: Why the existing workaround does not cover it / Design (transition_ticket_start gate type `transition`)
scenarios: An agent runs `verify_completion_start`, polls it to PASS, then calls `transition_ticket_start`. The daemon re-runs the full 9-11 minute verifier, which is a second billable pass.
An agent fires `verify_completion_start` and `transition_ticket_start` back-to-back. Two verifier runs for the same ticket and SHA proceed concurrently, under different dedup keys.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the sync `transition_ticket` close through `run_gate_singleflight` with the same `transition` key as `transition_ticket_start`, and state which key fields (ticket_id, target status) define it.
evidence: "the sync tool goes through `run_gate_singleflight` with the same key" (stated for review_code only)
"`transition_ticket_start` ... wraps the SAME derived `transition_ticket` tool ... and runs it on the gate daemon via `_start_gate_job`"
AC7: "de-dup protection applies to the new surfaces" — the existing sync transition_ticket close is not named.
findings.finding: De-dup does not cover the sync `transition_ticket` path. For `review_code`, the plan routes the sync tool through `run_gate_singleflight` with the same key as the starter. For `transition_ticket`, it only says the starter wraps the derived tool. The sync close keeps running the gate inline, outside the `transition` singleflight key. A sync close re-fire (the natural reaction to the timeout this bug describes) while a `transition_ticket_start` job is in flight therefore starts a second gate run. Two concurrent close attempts then race to append the transition.
scenarios: A caller fires `transition_ticket_start(close)`, then (or another agent) calls sync `transition_ticket(close)`, which times out and is re-fired. Up to three verifier passes run, and one loses with a ConcurrencyError.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the review_code design: have sync `transition_ticket` and `transition_ticket_start` share one body and one singleflight key `(transition, ticket_id, from->to)`, so a sync re-fire attaches to the in-flight daemon job.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Find out why the signed PASS was not reused at close (ref default mismatch HEAD vs origin/main, and/or reuse disabled when a pinned ticket_view exists), and add a fix plus an AC so a close after a current, ref-matching completion PASS reuses it with no LLM call.
evidence: Plan: 'Pre-computing the attestation does NOT make the close fast' (the plan records this as measured but never explains it)

close_autoresume.verify_with_auto_resume: `reused = None if ticket_view is not None else _reusable_attested_pass(...)`. close_precheck._completion_precheck always passes the captured ticket_view, so in pinned-view mode reuse is never tried

_reusable_attested_pass requires `resolve_ref(ref or 'HEAD') == signed_sha`. The transition_ticket spec says 'ref ... defaults to HEAD', while verify_completion_start's basis defaults to origin/main (_mcp_inflight.resolve_basis_sha). The measured cert was at origin/main f1fe7c6…, so a server checkout whose HEAD differs from origin/main can never reuse it
No AC requires a close after a current, matching completion PASS to skip the LLM
findings.finding: The plan does not find out why a signed completion PASS was not reused at close. It responds by making the close async, so every async close still runs a full new 9-11 minute billable verification even after verify_completion_start PASSed. The 'second billable gate pass' the Symptom complains about is not removed. It just moves to a daemon.
findings.location: Why the existing workaround does not cover it; Design → transition_ticket_start
scenarios: An agent follows the AGENTS.md guidance (verify_completion_start → PASS → transition_ticket_start). The close job pays for a second full verification because the close ref is HEAD, not origin/main, or because pinned-view mode is on.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the sync transition_ticket close path through run_gate_singleflight using the same 'transition' gate type and variant as transition_ticket_start, and extend AC7 to cover a re-fired sync close attaching to the in-flight run.
evidence: Symptom: 'the natural response is to re-fire the same call -- a second billable gate pass' and 'three successive attempts'
Design wraps 'the SAME derived transition_ticket tool' for the starter only. Unlike review_code, nothing says the sync transition_ticket goes through run_gate_singleflight with the 'transition' key
AC7 covers only 'the new surfaces'
findings.finding: The plan routes the sync review_code through run_gate_singleflight but leaves the sync transition_ticket close path without dedup. The Symptom's own failure mode, re-firing a sync close that timed out while the first one is still running on the server, still starts another billable verifier run. A sync close and a transition_ticket_start for the same close also never share a key.
scenarios: A client without the new starter (or an agent out of habit) calls sync transition_ticket(close), times out, and retries twice. That is three concurrent verifier runs, which is exactly the reported incident.
findings.suggested_fix: In the transition_ticket tool body, when target_status == 'closed', wrap the call in run_gate_singleflight('transition', ticket_id, ref=ref or 'HEAD', source='local'-equivalent basis, variant=<transition variant>, ...) so sync retries and async starts share one run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that AC4 uses a stub gate blocked on a test-controlled event: assert `gate_status` reports `running` after the handle returns, then release the event and poll to terminal.
evidence: "asserting the handle returned BEFORE the gate completed"
findings.finding: AC4 requires asserting that 'the handle returned BEFORE the gate completed' but gives no mechanism. A wall-clock threshold would be flaky. A deterministic approach (a fake gate blocked on an event or barrier that the test releases after receiving the handle) is not stated.
scenarios: A timing-based assertion passes on a fast CI box even with a blocking implementation, or flakes on a slow one.
findings.suggested_fix: Stub the gate callable to wait on a `threading.Event` (or file sentinel for the daemon), assert handle plus `status: running`, then set the event and poll `gate_status` to `passed`/`failed`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a check (or a recorded manual run on the ticket) in which an MCP client calls `transition_ticket_start` for a close, gets the handle well under 60s, and polls `gate_status` to a terminal state with the ticket status updated; or state why this is deferred.
evidence: The symptom is an MCP-client `-32001` timeout; no AC mentions an MCP client round-trip or the live gate.
findings.finding: No criterion exercises the real user-facing flow: closing a ticket over the actual MCP transport with a real completion verifier, within the ~60s client deadline. AC4 can pass entirely on stubbed gates, and the plan gives no rationale for omitting an end-to-end check.
scenarios: The daemon detaches correctly in unit tests but the MCP server's request handler still awaits something slow, so the real client still times out.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend AC3 to cover the schema's `gate_type`/`verdict` value sets (enum or documented values) for `code_review`, `transition`, and `applied`, and note the compatibility impact on existing `gate_status` consumers.
evidence: "A completed transition settles `passed` with verdict `applied`"
AC3: "the `GateRun` schema description name every starter"
Scope: "`schemas/gate_run.schema.json` ... describe only those two job kinds"
findings.finding: The plan introduces new `gate_type` values (`code_review`, `transition`) and a new verdict value (`applied`) but only commits to updating the `GateRun` schema DESCRIPTION. If `schemas/gate_run.schema.json` or `gate_status` consumers constrain `gate_type` or `verdict` to an enum (e.g. PASS/FAIL), the new job records would fail validation or break consumers. The plan neither acknowledges nor resolves this.
scenarios: A `gate_status` client that switches on verdict PASS/FAIL/BLOCK treats `applied` as unknown or failure.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a structured failure reason on `transition` jobs (e.g. `gate_fail` / `concurrency` / `provider_error`), mirroring review_code's structured provider-failure result.
evidence: "a refusal (gate FAIL, ConcurrencyError) settles `failed` with the message in `error`"
"so a provider failure is the same structured result on both" — stated only for review_code.
findings.finding: Failure classification for `transition` jobs lumps gate FAIL, ConcurrencyError, and (implicitly) provider/infrastructure errors into `failed` with a free-text `error`. A caller cannot tell a retry-worthy infrastructure failure from a substantive FAIL verdict. For `review_code` the plan explicitly makes provider failure a structured result; no equivalent is stated for `transition`.
scenarios: A provider outage during a close shows `failed`; the agent treats it as a FAIL verdict and starts unnecessary rework, or blindly retries a real FAIL.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Don't add a separate `GATE_TYPES_WITH_SIDECARS` constant. Keep the inline set, or derive it from the keys of `gate_runs._GATE_SIDECARS` so there is one registry of sidecar-bearing gate types.
evidence: A grep shows `_gate_sidecar_fields` is used only at _mcp_llm.py:221, so the new constant would have one consumer, well short of Rule-of-Three.
src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:179 already defines `_GATE_SIDECARS: dict[str, _SidecarSpec]` keyed by gate type, which is the authoritative registry `gate_status` uses (gate_runs.py:246).
The plan's own list puts `code_review` in the new constant but adds no `_GATE_SIDECARS` entry for it, so the two lists would disagree on day one.
findings.finding: The new `GATE_TYPES_WITH_SIDECARS` constant would have one call site and duplicates a registry that already exists, `gate_runs._GATE_SIDECARS`. That gives two independent lists of 'gate types with sidecars' that can drift.
scenarios: A future gate gets added to one list and not the other, and `gate_status` sidecar readability quietly differs from what the daemon recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_gate_sidecar_fields`, test `gate_type in rebar.llm.gate_runs._GATE_SIDECARS` (or a public alias of its keys) instead of adding a new constant.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Register `transition_ticket_start` from inside `register_write_tools` (_mcp_writes.py), which already skips read-only servers and hosts `run_workflow`, or state why a separate registrar is needed. If kept, require that build_server wraps it in `_instrumented(...)`.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:16-24: `register_write_tools` returns early on `ctx.readonly()` and calls `derive_tools(mcp, ctx, "write")`, which is where the derived `transition_ticket` spec (registrar="write", _mcp_tool_specs.py:655-657) gets registered.

The same file defines `run_workflow`, an async daemon-backed write tool returning `{run_id, ticket_id, status:'running'}`. That is precedent for putting an async write starter in this registrar. The file is only about 113 lines, so no complexity cap forces a split.

build_server calls exactly three registrars (mcp_server.py:513-515), and scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:87-112 enumerates exactly those three. AC6 has to add 'must enumerate the new registrar' only because a fourth registration path is being created.
Plan: "skipped on a read-only server, like the write tools"
findings.finding: `transition_ticket_start` gets a new module (`src/rebar/_mcp_ticket_async.py`) and a new registration call in `mcp_server.build_server` that is 'skipped on a read-only server, like the write tools'. findings.finding: The plan builds a custom async-job-and-poll layer (`*_start` tools plus `gate_status`) to get around the MCP request timeout. It never considers the protocol's own solutions to the same problem: the MCP Tasks primitive (SEP-1686, in the 2025-11-25 spec, call-now/fetch-later for any request) and `notifications/progress`, which some clients use to reset the request timeout. The installed MCP SDK already includes both. Since the plan widens a repo-specific workaround to every gate surface, it should say why it isn't adopting the protocol mechanism, or using it alongside.
scenarios: A client that supports MCP Tasks could run `transition_ticket` as a task natively. The repo-specific `transition_ticket_start` / `gate_status` pair then becomes an extra, non-standard surface that agents have to learn from AGENTS.md.
A future maintainer adopts SEP-1686 and finds two overlapping async mechanisms with different dedup and handle semantics.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one paragraph under Design: 'Alternatives: MCP Tasks (SEP-1686, spec 2025-11-25) and progress notifications that reset the client timeout address the same -32001 failure, but client support is uneven (some clients ignore progress and hardcode 60s), and the repo already ships `review_plan_start`/`verify_completion_start` on the job/`gate_status` contract. We extend that contract for consistency and revisit native Tasks once target clients support it.'

findings.finding: The transition job's verdict has no defined place where it is produced. The plan says 'A completed transition settles `passed` with verdict `applied`', but the only `_terminal_from_result` change it specifies is the code-review unwrap. The transition_ticket tool returns `{ticket_id, from, to, newly_unblocked}` (plus push/warning post hooks) and has no `verdict` key, so the existing rule would record verdict=None. On refusal, `_spawn_gate_daemon` puts str(exc) into both `verdict` and `error`, so a failed transition's `verdict` is free text, not a defined value.
scenarios: An executor wires transition_ticket_start through `_start_gate_job` unchanged; gate_status then shows passed/verdict=null, and AC3's 'verdict' for `transition` is never met.
A gate-FAIL close shows verdict=<long exception text>, which a client matching on a verdict enum can't parse.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the transition_ticket_start work closure wrap the tool result as {**result, "verdict": "applied"}, and have it catch the gate-refusal and ConcurrencyError exceptions and return {"error": msg, "verdict": "refused"} so the daemon's generic exception arm isn't used for expected refusals. Document {applied, refused} in the gate_status docstring and in the GateRun schema description.
